title: Bayer licenses Phase I bispecific ADC from Hansoh Pharma in US$3.25B deal | HealthCare Middle East & Africa - No.1 Health & Pharma Manufacturing Industry Publication
summary: Bayer will hold exclusive development and commercialisation rights worldwide, except in mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan.
thbAction: Use the article as an entry point to pitch THB's commercial visibility layer for territory planning, account prioritization, and next-best-action for pharma leadership teams.
contentHtml:
GERMANY—Bayer has signed a global licensing agreement potentially worth US$3.25 billion with China’s Hansoh Pharma to develop and commercialize HS-20122, a Phase I antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) candidate targeting solid tumours.

Under the agreement, Bayer will pay Hansoh Pharma US$150 million upfront, with a further US$3.1 billion available through milestones tied to clinical development, regulatory approvals and commercialisation.

Hansoh will also receive tiered royalties on future net sales.

Bayer will hold exclusive development and commercialisation rights worldwide, except in mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan.

The transaction remains subject to regulatory clearance, including antitrust approval.

ADC targets EGFR and c-MET

HS-20122 is a bispecific ADC designed to target epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and mesenchymal-epithelial transition factor (c-MET), two proteins associated with tumour progression and treatment resistance in certain cancers.

The candidate combines targeted delivery with a cytotoxic payload intended to selectively kill cancer cells expressing the two targets. Hansoh is developing HS-20122 for solid tumours, including non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

Clinical findings evaluating the candidate’s safety and efficacy in patients with advanced solid tumours, including NSCLC, were presented at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress.

Bayer expands precision oncology pipeline

Bayer’s licensing agreement builds on its strategy to expand its oncology pipeline through targeted therapies, including ADCs.

The collaboration combines Hansoh’s ADC development programme with Bayer’s global clinical development, manufacturing and commercialisation capabilities.

Juergen Eckhardt, head of business development and licensing at Bayer’s Pharmaceuticals Division, said the company would advance HS-20122 alongside Hansoh as it pursues new treatment approaches for lung cancer and other solid tumours.

He highlighted the continued need for treatments that improve efficacy and tolerability for people living with lung cancer, noting that the programme supports Bayer’s precision oncology strategy by developing therapies designed to deliver cytotoxic agents more selectively to tumour cells.

The deal also comes as Bayer expands its pharmaceutical manufacturing footprint.

Last month, the company announced plans to invest US$2.2 billion in a new pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in Ohio, USA.
